FR12 hack = route the spine through native's kernel TO PASS A PARITY METRIC while OUR deliverable kernel stays unchanged/broken and the real compute happens elsewhere. The "FLASH-for-branchless-spine" candidate is NOT that: I verified in fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py that on a pure spine `is_single_spine()` (parent==[-1,0,1,2,..]) the ancestry mask `strict[i,j]=1 for j in ancestors(i)` IS exactly the lower-triangular causal pattern, and in fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py:63-67 the bias application is `+0.0` (IEEE x+0.0==x for finite x) on ancestor/self and `=-INFINITY` (== stock causal mask) above-diagonal. So a branchless chain GENUINELY has bias==causal: computing its attention via stock causal FA2 is the *correct op for that input*, not a route-around. The deliverable is unchanged; branch rows (non-causal bias) still use the tree-bias fork. That is the legitimate side of the FR12 distinction, correctly drawn in the doc.

DECISIVE caveat that the verdict turns on: candidate 2 is about ATTENTION, but the proven +2 CARRIER is the GDN recurrent SCAN (q1: 9.14x, 89% input-drift). A FLASH route can only touch attention; it CANNOT reach the GDN scan. So spine-FLASH is a structural null regardless of legitimacy — it cannot close the +2.
